# RETRO: #12978 follow-up (team 4)

## What worked
- Neutral brief with pinned read-only worktrees and fully materialized objects; both reviewers stayed in their own directories.
- Targeted cross-examination settled the first-enable disagreement (packaging evidence) and upgraded the switch-helper residual from "cosmetic" to "minor".
- Bindings dumped with an argument-preserving stub exposed the local-mode regression the PR test cannot see.

## Process deviations (recorded, no impact on technical conclusions)
- Coordinator policy read of assignment WORKFLOW.md lines 316-387 returned 72 lines in one tool response, exceeding the 60-line aggregate bound. Content was read completely; no fixture work had started.
- Initial partial-clone (`--filter=blob:none`) meant diff/log reads lazily fetched blobs into the assignment-owned clone before full materialization. Owned, disposable clone; not shared source. First refetch attempt used a wrong ref name (master) and failed (intake/refetch.err preserved); second attempt succeeded.
- The mandated Opus prompt text does not repeat the first-call rules; they were placed at the top of brief.md instead.

## Improvements
- Earlier R3 overstated first-enable by not checking /etc/skel seeding: check packaging and seeding docs before claiming a directory is missing on fresh installs.
- Suggest a reusable md-to-HTML helper in review-team (none installed; ad hoc converter used).

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the previous review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5806831484) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12978#issuecomment-5815867586), checked at `ab8e77e0cfd7`.

**Outcome:** most previous findings are fixed. One new change regresses local mode (toggle off): SUPER+SHIFT+N no longer follows the moved window. Focus still leaves the current monitor when the Lua hook syncs other monitors, and two hotplug edge cases remain. The previous "bar can miss the first enable" finding is withdrawn.

| Previous finding | Status at `ab8e77e0cfd7` |
|---|---|
| Disconnected monitors reset the desktop to slot 1 | **Resolved** in `omarchy-ensure-workspaces`. The switch helper still uses disconnected monitors (see below) |
| Move helper fallback unreachable | **Resolved** |
| Default keybindings bypass the new commands | **Resolved** for global mode, with a new local-mode regression (see below) |
| `monitor-base-test.sh`, `bin-style-test.sh`, missing `omarchy:hidden` | **Resolved.** All pass at this head in an isolated run, and fail at `13597029b25a` |
| Optional test: run the real move helper | **Resolved.** The new move test fails against the `caff3e03ef34` helper |
| Focus moves off the current monitor | **Still present** through the Lua hook. The switch helper is fixed |
| Workspace IDs above 99 stop syncing | **Partly resolved.** The bar is fixed; the Lua bound goes stale after hotplug |
| Bar can miss the first enable | **Withdrawn** (see below) |

**Verified:** every finding from the first two reviews remains resolved. All seven test files this PR adds pass at this head, and the four new ones each fail against `13597029b25a` on the case they target.

## New in this revision

### SUPER+SHIFT+N no longer follows the window in local mode

[`tiling.lua`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ab8e77e0cfd7aed23ee528db88217d4e1fbbeee8/default/hypr/bindings/tiling.lua#L21-L29) now binds both SUPER+SHIFT+N and SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+N to `omarchy-move-window-to-aw N`. With the toggle off, [that wrapper](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ab8e77e0cfd7aed23ee528db88217d4e1fbbeee8/bin/omarchy-move-window-to-aw#L26-L30) always passes `follow = false`.

```text
Bindings evaluated with a recording stub, toggle off:
                    base                                   this head
SUPER+SHIFT+2       window.move({ workspace = "2" })       window.move({ workspace = "2", follow = false })
SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+2   window.move({ workspace = "2",         window.move({ workspace = "2", follow = false })
                                  follow = false })
```

In Hyprland 0.56.2 a move without `follow = false` switches to the target workspace with the window (`LuaBindingsDispatchers.cpp`, `ConfigActions.cpp` `moveToWorkspace`).

**Impact:** every user on the default local mode loses "move window and follow" on SUPER+SHIFT+N. It now does the same as the silent binding, while the keybindings menu still lists them as different actions. `workspace-global-bindings-test.sh` passes with this change because it only checks that some `hyprctl` call happens in local mode. Dispatcher-level and source result, not observed in a native session.

**Suggested change:** keep base behavior when the flag is off. For example, leave `tiling.lua` unchanged and have `workspace-global.lua` rebind the workspace keys with `o.rebind` (toggles load after the bindings), or give the move wrapper a follow/silent argument whose local branch matches the base dispatchers.

**Cleanup:** the new repository-root `install.sh` is a separate installer for testers. Nothing in Omarchy's install or update path runs it or packages it. It uses `sudo` to overwrite files under `/usr/share/omarchy`, copies the helpers into `~/.local/bin`, and appends a PATH line to `~/.bashrc`/`~/.zshrc`. Its header still describes `caff3e03`. Dropping it from the PR (keeping it in a separate branch or gist) avoids shipping it.

## Still present

### Lua hook still moves focus off the current monitor

The switch helper now dispatches the focused monitor last, and focus stays on it. The [Lua hook](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ab8e77e0cfd7aed23ee528db88217d4e1fbbeee8/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L270-L299) refocuses the originating monitor only when that monitor is not on the target workspace. When the event comes from that monitor's own switch, it is already on target, so it is skipped. Each dispatch to another monitor then focuses that monitor and warps the pointer (`ConfigActions.cpp`, `changeWorkspace`), and Hyprland does not re-enter a running `hl.on` handler.

```text
Modelled from Hyprland 0.56.2 source, not a native run:
                                          13597029b25a   this head
switch helper, SUPER+2 on eDP-1 (2 mon)   HDMI-A-1       eDP-1
Lua hook only, ws 2 on eDP-1 (2 mon)      HDMI-A-1       HDMI-A-1
Lua hook only, ws 2 on eDP-1 (3 mon)      DP-2           DP-2
```

**Impact:** workspace changes that reach only the hook (SUPER+TAB, SUPER+SHIFT+TAB, SUPER+CTRL+TAB, SUPER+scroll) still leave keyboard focus and the pointer on another monitor. The reply's "focused monitor last in both the bash helper and the Lua hook" holds for the helper only.

**Suggested change:** in the hook, record the focused monitor before dispatching and refocus it afterwards (for example `hl.dsp.focus({ monitor = <name> })`), rather than ordering by whether it needs a change.

### Hotplug edge cases in the switch helper and Lua bound

- [`omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ab8e77e0cfd7aed23ee528db88217d4e1fbbeee8/bin/omarchy-hyprland-workspace-global-switch#L68) still iterates every saved base, including monitors that are no longer connected. In the model the final slot is correct, but the connected monitor passes through extra workspace switches first (for example `eDP-1 -> 12 -> 2`), and a missing workspace is briefly created on the focused monitor.
- The Lua [`ws_id_upper_bound`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/ab8e77e0cfd7aed23ee528db88217d4e1fbbeee8/default/hypr/toggles/workspace-global.lua#L234-L240) is computed once per config evaluation. The `monitor.added` handler refreshes the bases but not the bound, so a hotplugged monitor with base 90 or higher (the headless-output case) does not sync until the next reload.

**Impact:** extra workspace animations and IPC events per disconnected saved monitor on each switch, and no sync on high-base outputs added since the last reload. Both are modelled from source.

**Suggested change:** filter the switch helper by `hyprctl monitors -j`, as `omarchy-ensure-workspaces` now does. Drop the Lua upper bound (the bar no longer uses one) or recompute it in the `monitor.added` handler.

## Withdrawn

**Bar can miss the first enable on a fresh setup:** this was wrong, including at `13597029b25a`. `omarchy-settings` seeds `~/.local/state/omarchy/toggles/hypr/` through `/etc/skel` (`docs/file-layout.md`), and the Quattro upgrade creates it for existing users, so the watched directory exists before the first toggle. The root `install.sh` change is therefore not needed for this.

**Optional test improvement:** `workspace-global-bindings-test.sh` passes with the SUPER+SHIFT+N regression above. Asserting the local-mode dispatch for SUPER+SHIFT+N (following) and SUPER+SHIFT+ALT+N (silent) would catch it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** pinned-source inspection of `ab8e77e0cfd7` against `13597029b25a` and base, with Hyprland 0.56.2, hyprutils, Quickshell and Qt source, and Omarchy packaging for the withdrawn finding. Isolated command runs covered the repository test suites at head and base, the new tests against `13597029b25a`, the move helper, the default bindings under a recording stub, and a stub Hyprland Lua model of focus and hotplug behavior. No native Hyprland, bar rendering, multi-monitor, hotplug or keybinding test was run. The focus, hotplug and follow results are source-derived or modelled.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, with independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments of this revision and targeted cross-checks of points on which they differed. Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
